gen-gf-grenze-gf-lexend-exa: Grenze has barely any ascender height above its x-height. It carves out a literary, stencil-cut voice, while Lexend Exa handles the reading itself, its curves wide and stubby-limbed with an unvarying line.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-lexend-mega: Refined and a bit literary, Grenze keeps its strokes close together with only mild thick-to-thin shifts. And Lexend Mega moves along behind it in one constant line, tall-bodied and open, so a long read feels approachable.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-lexend-peta: Stencil-cut, bookish, slightly stern: that's Grenze, with curves thickened like a reed pen's. Lexend Peta works against it with thread-like strokes and wide-mouthed c shapes, so the two sit together with a clear difference.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws a single plotter-pen line, with open curves and letters spaced like stepping stones. Next to Grenze, its sturdy stems give way to lighter curves, and that clash is the point.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-lexend-zetta: Literary and tightly set, Grenze keeps even its thinnest strokes from going spindly. Lexend Zetta then offers ribbon-cut lines of constant width, with tall small letters spread wide, where diagonals match horizontals.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-montserrat-alternates: Grenze's ascenders barely clear its x-height, giving it a stencil-cut, refined look with moderate contrast between stems and bars. Make it small and Montserrat Alternates, with its thin-free chalkboard lowercase, would overpower it.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-gambetta: Tall, bold, and unmistakable: Gugi's lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, with stems and arcs locked together. But Gambetta settles in behind it with a lower lowercase and gently tapering strokes, so a long passage feels bookish and graceful.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-abyssinica-sil: Gugi draws wirelike strokes of one thickness, with tall lowercase and counters that flow open at the terminals. Abyssinica SIL gives the body its brushed-watercolor shift in weight, which is where Gugi's boldness gives way to quiet.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-cambo: Gugi's terminals are cut open so its counters flow outward, framed by strokes of identical width. Cambo follows with a short step from lowercase to capital and arches that thin gently, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-fanwood-text: Fanwood Text has a large-eyed lowercase and gently swelling curves, set under Gugi's tall, tapering-free heading letters. Long paragraphs would move steadily, with weight changes that stay quiet.
